note: The single source of truth for what is left before Catch Comics launches. Edit this file, reload Launch Control. Every claim here was measured on 2026-09-22 — see `evidence` on each item.

targets.rationale: Two blockers remain and both are hours of work, not weeks. Soft launch two days out leaves one clear day of production soak after the last fix. Public launch five days after that is enough to see whether real shoppers search, click and buy — and short enough that it cannot quietly become another month.

verdict.because: One production defect priced the wrong book, fixed today but not yet deployed. Everything else on the customer journey is proven.

blockers.title: Ship the eBay edition gate to production
blockers.why: Production is serving the wrong book as the cheapest offer. For Hellboy Omnibus Vol. 1, 7 of 8 eBay offers were a different book — Vol. 2, Vol. 4 and a B.P.R.D. title — and the page quoted "from £14.42" for a book that costs £19.36. A shopper following the cheapest offer bought the wrong comic. This is the one defect that breaks the site's whole purpose.
blockers.done: The Hellboy Omnibus Vol. 1 page on production lists only Hellboy Omnibus Vol. 1 offers, and npm run audit:ebay-relevance shows 0 rails emptied.
blockers.evidence: Fixed, tested and verified on localhost 2026-09-22: lib/listings/productRelevance.ts, 28/28 unit assertions, calibrated against live production offers. Awaiting the Vercel deploy from this commit.

blockers.title: Confirm product pages do not scroll sideways on a phone
blockers.why: The 2026-09-01 review recorded every product page rendering 644px wide at a 390px viewport, on production, with the header search form overflowing. Most comic shoppers are on a phone. If it is real it is a serious mobile failure on the core journey; if it is stale it costs one test run to close.
blockers.done: A Playwright assertion at 390px proves documentElement.scrollWidth <= viewport width on home, search and a product page — or the overflow is found and fixed.
blockers.evidence: UNVERIFIED this session: the in-app browser pane cannot emulate a viewport narrower than 644px, so neither confirmation nor refutation was possible. Browser Trust's mobile-chromium project passes 9 tests but asserts nothing about horizontal overflow.

waiting.title: Amazon Creators API eligibility
waiting.detail: Amazon returns AssociateNotEligible. Credentials, OAuth, token caching and the affiliate tag are all proven working — no code change can lift this. It needs ~10 qualifying sales in the trailing 30 days, which needs real shoppers, which needs launch.

waiting.title: Travelling Man price refresh completing
waiting.detail: A price-verify write run has been going since 19:07 UTC, 0 errors. Freshness is already safe — launch health reports 0 stale listings and Travelling Man last seen 2026-09-21 — so this is a top-up, not a race.

waiting.title: Retailer coverage beyond Travelling Man
waiting.detail: Waterstones, Wordery, WHSmith, Zavvi and AbeBooks feeds stopped refreshing in May–July and their listings aged out. Comparison depth is 0 products at 2+ stored retailers. The site's copy is already honest about this ("Cheapest tracked retailer — eBay may be lower") and eBay adds a live second source at view time, so it does not block launch. It is the main post-launch growth job.

gates.label: Amazon
gates.detail: Blocked by Amazon's own eligibility gate. Does not block launch.

amazon.apiDetail: AssociateNotEligible — credentials valid, OAuth succeeds, token cached, tag catchcomics-21 correct.
amazon.theRealProblem: There is no Amazon link on the main product page. PricingPanel — the only component with a tagged "Search Amazon UK" link — renders solely on the legacy /comic/[id] route. The product pages that produced all 307 clickouts show Amazon only from stored listings, and there are 0 of those. So no amount of traffic can currently produce a qualifying sale, and the founder estimate of 5 predates the Rainforest retirement. Waiting does not fix this; a link does.
amazon.afterEligibility: The client, adapter, env wiring and bounded probe already exist. What remains is the importer that turns a getItems response into listings — ISBN/ASIN-anchored, condition honest, freshness rules unchanged — plus a dry run and founder approval before the first live write.

afterLaunch.title: Description and synopsis coverage
afterLaunch.detail: 68.5% of listed products have no description at all. A free Open Library / Google Books ISBN backfill is the plan-level fix; it writes canonical_products so it needs approval and a dry run.

afterLaunch.title: Creator credits and a creator index
afterLaunch.detail: 93% of products store no creators, and /api/search has no creator matching, so clickable credits would land on junk. Needs a creator route — hands-off search SQL, plan first.

afterLaunch.title: Merge fix/product-page-consolidated
afterLaunch.detail: Contents rail, 8-line description clamp and eBay row collapse, all verified locally on 2026-09-01 and never merged. Real improvements, but shipping nothing keeps the status quo honest, so it is not a blocker. Merge this branch — NOT the repair/product-* branches, whose rail shipped false contents.

afterLaunch.title: Retailer feed revival
afterLaunch.detail: Bring back Waterstones, Wordery, WHSmith, Zavvi, AbeBooks so comparison depth stops being 1.

afterLaunch.title: Comparison depth as a real feature
afterLaunch.detail: 0 products currently show two stored retailers. Until feeds return, eBay is the second source.

afterLaunch.title: Cover coverage
afterLaunch.detail: 20.3% of products have an R2 cover; 94,141 have none.

afterLaunch.title: Collection system, accounts, social, recommendations
afterLaunch.detail: Explicitly frozen. Nothing here may pre-empt launch.

afterLaunch.title: Advanced SEO programme
afterLaunch.detail: Basics are in place — robots, sitemap, canonicals, OG all returning 200. Anything beyond that waits.

softLaunch.cohort: 20–30 real UK comic buyers. People who actually buy comics, not friends being polite. Reddit r/comicbooks and r/graphicnovels regulars, a local shop's customers, two or three comics Discords.
softLaunch.ask: Find a comic you actually want and tell me if the price is right.
measure: clickouts and distinct visitors — npm run launch:signal
which comics people search for and click
any wrong-product or wrong-price report (P1, fix immediately)
whether anyone completes a purchase at the retailer
softLaunch.doNot: Do not ask anyone to buy through Amazon to manufacture qualifying sales.

triage.note: First week after public launch, only these two classes get worked on. Everything else is backlog.
triage.p0: Site unusable · data loss · security · cost runaway
triage.p1: Wrong product · broken retailer flow · major mobile failure
